raw_text:
Below is a progressive, minimalist 12‑week strength program designed for a true beginner training in a small flat with only a yoga mat and a doorway pull-up bar. It builds total-body strength using bodyweight movements, emphasizes impeccable technique and progressive overload, and provides clear weekly structure, session details, and progression targets. It’s split into three phases to develop foundations, then add volume and intensity, and finally consolidate with higher-skill variations. Sessions are 3 nonconsecutive days/week (e.g., Mon–Wed–Fri). Optional brief “Grease the Groove” pull-up practice and easy mobility on off days.

Global notes
- Warm-up (8–10 min before every session):
  - 2–3 min light cardio (jumping jacks, high knees, brisk in-place march)
  - Dynamic mobility: shoulder CARs, arm circles, scapular shrugs/hangs, hip circles, 10 bodyweight good mornings, 10 deep squat pries
  - Movement prep: 1 easy set for each main pattern (e.g., 5 easy push-ups, 5 air squats, 10s hollow hold)
- Tempo: Use controlled lowers to build strength. Notation example: 3–1–1 means 3s down, 1s pause, 1s up.
- Rest: 60–90s between sets early; 90–150s as efforts get closer to failure.
- Intensity: Leave 1–2 reps in reserve on main sets unless noted as AMRAP (as many reps as possible, technical limit).
- Progression priorities:
  1) Add reps to the prescribed ranges
  2) Then add sets (if indicated)
  3) Then advance the variation (e.g., incline to full push-up)
- Pull-up bar safety: Ensure doorframe and bar are secure before every set. Use a neutral grip if available. Keep neck neutral; no aggressive kipping.
- Core tension: Ribcage stacked over pelvis; glutes lightly engaged on planks/hollow work.
- Optional extras on off days:
  - 2–3 easy sets of scapular pull-ups (5–8 reps) and dead hangs (20–40s total) to build pulling capacity
  - 10–15 min walk or easy cardio for recovery

Phase overview
- Phase 1 (Weeks 1–4): Foundations and capacity. Build baseline strength, positions, and joint tolerance.
- Phase 2 (Weeks 5–8): Progressive overload. Increase volume/intensity, introduce harder variations and isometric work.
- Phase 3 (Weeks 9–12): Consolidation and skill. Push density/quality, harder unilateral and lever variations, and specific rep targets.

Movement menu by pattern
- Push: Wall/incline push-up → knee push-up → full push-up → diamond/archer/Eccentric push-ups
- Pull: Dead hang → scapular pull-up → flexed-arm hang → slow eccentric pull-ups → bandless assisted (jump/foot-on-chair) pull-ups → full pull-ups
- Squat/lunge: Air squat (with pauses/tempos) → split squat → reverse lunge → Bulgarian split squat (rear foot elevated on couch/chair) → shrimp squat progression
- Hinge: Hip hinge good mornings → glute bridge → single-leg glute bridge → hip thrust (shoulders on couch) → single-leg hip thrust
- Core (anterior): Dead bug → hollow hold/rock progression → RKC plank → push-up position shoulder taps
- Core (anti-rotation/oblique): Side plank progressions → dead bug with reach → hollow side body holds
- Posterior shoulder/scapula: Face pulls can’t be loaded; use Y-T-W prone, scapular push-ups, wall slides

Weekly structure (3 days/week)
- Day A: Push emphasis + Squat + Core
- Day B: Pull emphasis + Hinge + Core/Scapula
- Day C: Total body mix + Unilateral focus + Core

PHASE 1: Weeks 1–4 (Foundations)
Goals: Groove technique, accumulate submax volume, build joint integrity, start vertical pulling capacity with hangs and eccentrics.

Week 1
- Day A
  - Incline push-up on countertop or sturdy table, 3×8–10, 3–1–1 tempo
  - Air squat, 3×12, 2–1–1 tempo; sit-to-stand depth if needed
  - RKC plank, 3×20–30s (max tension, glute squeeze)
  - Optional: Prone Y-T-W, 2×8 each
- Day B
  - Dead hang from bar, 3×20–30s total per set (can break into mini-sets)
  - Scapular pull-ups, 3×6–8, slow and controlled
  - Glute bridge, 3×12–15, 2–2–1 tempo
  - Hollow hold tuck, 3×15–20s
- Day C
  - Knee push-up, 3×8–10, 3–1–1
  - Split squat (bodyweight), 3×8/side, 2–1–1
  - Side plank (bent knees if needed), 3×20–30s/side
  - Scapular push-ups, 2×10–12

Week 2
- Day A
  - Incline push-up (slightly lower surface), 4×8–10
  - Air squat with 2s pause at bottom, 3×10
  - RKC plank, 3×25–35s
  - Prone Y-T-W, 2×10 each
- Day B
  - Dead hang, 3×25–35s total
  - Scapular pull-ups, 3×8–10
  - Hip thrust (shoulders on couch), 3×12, 2–1–1
  - Hollow hold tuck→one-leg extended if able, 3×20–25s
- Day C
  - Knee push-up, 4×8–12
  - Reverse lunge, 3×8–10/side
  - Side plank (straight legs if able), 3×25–35s/side
  - Shoulder taps (high plank), 2×10/side

Week 3
- Day A
  - Incline push-up lower again or transition to full push-up for first set, 4×8–12
  - Air squat, 3×12–15, 2–1–1
  - RKC plank, 3×30–40s
  - Prone Y-T-W, 2×10–12
- Day B
  - Eccentric pull-up: Jump to chin over bar, 3–5s lower, 4×3–5
  - Flexed-arm hang (chin over bar), 3×10–20s
  - Hip thrust, 4×10–12
  - Hollow hold (one leg extended), 3×25–35s
- Day C
  - Push-up (mix full and knee as needed), 4×AMRAP to RIR 1–2
  - Split squat, 4×8–10/side
  - Side plank, 3×30–40s/side
  - Scapular push-ups, 2×12–15

Week 4
- Day A
  - Full push-up (elevate if needed for target reps), 4×8–12, 3–1–1
  - Air squat with 3s eccentric + 1s pause, 4×10–12
  - RKC plank, 3×35–45s
  - Prone Y-T-W, 2×12 each
- Day B
  - Eccentric pull-up, 5×3–4 at 4–5s down
  - Flexed-arm hang, 4×15–25s
  - Single-leg glute bridge, 3×10–12/side
  - Hollow body hold (both legs extended if able), 3×20–30s
- Day C
  - Push-up, 5×AMRAP to RIR 1–2
  - Reverse lunge, 4×10–12/side
  - Side plank with top-leg raise (if ready), 3×25–35s/side
  - Shoulder taps, 3×10–12/side

PHASE 2: Weeks 5–8 (Progressive Overload)
Goals: Increase intensity, introduce unilateral challenges, build toward first strict pull-up, strengthen midline.

Week 5
- Day A
  - Push-up, 5×8–12; last set AMRAP (technical)
  - Tempo squat 3–1–1, 4×12
  - RKC plank, 3×40–50s
  - Prone Y-T-W, 2×12–15
- Day B
  - Assisted pull-up (foot lightly on a chair in front), 5×4–6, 2–1–1 tempo; minimize leg help
  - Eccentric pull-up, 3×3–4 at 5s down
  - Hip thrust, 4×12–15
  - Hollow hold, 3×25–35s
- Day C
  - Close-grip push-up (hands just inside shoulders), 4×6–10
  - Bulgarian split squat (rear foot on couch), 4×8–10/side
  - Side plank, 3×35–45s/side
  - Shoulder taps, 3×12–15/side

Week 6
- Day A
  - Push-up with 1s pause at bottom, 5×6–10
  - Squat to 1.5 reps (down–up halfway–down–up), 4×8–10
  - RKC plank, 3×45–55s
  - Scapular push-ups, 2×15
- Day B
  - Assisted pull-up, 6×4–6 (aim for less assistance each week)
  - Flexed-arm hang (overhand), 4×20–30s
  - Single-leg hip thrust, 4×10–12/side
  - Hollow rock (tucked→full), 3×10–20 reps
- Day C
  - Pike or decline push-up (feet on couch) if strong enough; else standard, 4×6–10
  - Bulgarian split squat, 4×10–12/side
  - Side plank with reach-through, 3×10/side
  - Dead bug, 3×8–10/side slow

Week 7
- Day A
  - Push-up, 5×AMRAP to RIR 1–2; add diamond push-ups for last set if 15+ reps
  - Squat with 3s eccentric + 2s pause, 4×8–10
  - RKC plank, 3×50–60s
  - Prone Y-T-W, 2×15 each
- Day B
  - Assisted pull-up, 5×5–7
  - Eccentric pull-up, 3×3–5 at 5–6s down
  - Hip thrust, 5×10–12 (hard squeeze)
  - Hollow hold, 3×30–40s
- Day C
  - Archer push-up prep (shift weight side to side in bottom), 4×6–8/side, or close-grip if not ready
  - Reverse lunge with 2s pause at bottom, 4×10–12/side
  - Side plank, 3×45–60s/side
  - Shoulder taps, 3×15–20/side

Week 8
- Day A
  - Decline/pike push-up, 4×6–10
  - Squat 1.5 reps, 4×10
  - Hollow body hold, 3×30–40s
  - Scapular push-ups, 2×15–20
- Day B
  - Test strict pull-up: After warm-up, attempt singles for up to 5 attempts with 2–3 min rest; if successful, do 3–5 total singles. If not, continue:
  - Assisted pull-up, 5×5–7
  - Flexed-arm hang (chin over), 3×25–35s
  - Single-leg hip thrust, 4×12/side
- Day C
  - Push-up, 5×10–15 (or AMRAP with RIR 1–2)
  - Bulgarian split squat, 5×8–10/side
  - Side plank with top-leg raise, 3×30–45s/side
  - Dead bug with bandless “pulldown” (arms overhead hold), 3×10/side

PHASE 3: Weeks 9–12 (Consolidation and Skill)
Goals: Achieve first strict pull-up(s), raise push-up numbers, strengthen single-leg patterns, and harden trunk stability. Introduce density and isometric finishers.

Week 9
- Day A
  - Push-up ladder: 6–8 sets of 6–10 with 60–75s rest (same reps each set)
  - Squat: 3s down + 1s pause, 5×10
  - RKC plank, 3×50–60s
  - Prone Y-T-W, 2×15–20
- Day B
  - Strict pull-up practice: 6–8 singles (or assisted singles) with perfect form; 2–3 min rest
  - Eccentric pull-up, 3×3–4 at 6s down
  - Hip thrust, 5×12
  - Hollow rock, 3×15–25
- Day C
  - Diamond or close-grip push-up, 4×8–12
  - Bulgarian split squat with 2s pause, 4×10/side
  - Side plank long lever (elbow slightly forward), 3×30–45s/side
  - Shoulder taps, 3×20/side

Week 10
- Day A
  - Push-up: 4 sets to RIR 1, 1 set AMRAP (technical)
  - Squat 1.5 reps, 5×8–10
  - Hollow body hold, 3×35–45s
  - Scapular push-ups, 2×20
- Day B
  - Pull-up density block: 10 min EMOM
    - Min 1–5: 1 strict pull-up or 1 assisted rep + 3–5s eccentric
    - Min 6–10: same or drop to eccentric single
  - Single-leg hip thrust, 4×12–15/side
  - Flexed-arm hang (overhand), 3×25–35s
- Day C
  - Pike/decline push-up, 4×8–10
  - Reverse lunge, 4×12/side
  - Side plank with reach-through, 3×12/side
  - Dead bug slow, 3×10/side

Week 11
- Day A
  - Push-up: Add mechanical drop set each set (e.g., decline → standard → knee, with minimal rest): 4 rounds of 6–8 decline + 6–10 standard + 8–12 knee
  - Squat: 3s eccentric + 2s pause, 4×8–10
  - RKC plank, 3×60–70s
- Day B
  - Pull-up test: Up to 5 attempts for max singles; rest 2–3 min between. Then:
  - Assisted pull-up, 4×5–7
  - Eccentric pull-up, 2×3 at 6–8s down
  - Hip thrust, 4×12–15
  - Hollow rock, 3×20–30
- Day C
  - Archer push-up prep or pseudo planche lean push-up (small lean), 4×6–8
  - Bulgarian split squat, 5×8–10/side
  - Side plank long lever, 3×40–50s/side
  - Shoulder taps, 3×20–25/side

Week 12 (Deload/Test and Consolidate)
- Reduce total volume ~30–40% but keep intensity. Celebrate milestones and set next goals.
- Day A
  - Push-up, 3×AMRAP to RIR 1–2 (aim to set a rep PR on first or second set)
  - Air squat, 3×15 smooth (easy pace)
  - Hollow hold, 2×30–40s
- Day B
  - Pull-up test: Warm up hangs and scaps; attempt best-quality singles. Record max number of strict singles you can accumulate in 10–12 min with 2–3 min rests.
  - Hip thrust, 3×10 easy
  - Light scapular work 2×12
- Day C
  - Favorite push-up variation, 3×submax
  - Bulgarian split squat, 3×8/side easy pace
  - Side plank, 2×40s/side
- End-of-phase notes: If 1–3 strict pull-ups achieved, next block will build small-rep clusters. If not yet there, continue assisted + eccentric mix and hangs; you’re close.

Progression and scaling details
- Push-ups:
  - If sets are too easy: lower incline or elevate feet; add pauses; slow eccentrics; mechanical drop sets.
  - If too hard: increase incline height or do knee push-ups to complete prescribed volume.
- Pull-ups:
  - Use minimal foot support on a chair. Think “knees as scale” to just float your body. Gradually reduce pressure.
  - If no pull-up yet: blend 2–3 weekly exposures of eccentric reps plus isometric hangs.
  - Keep shoulders depressed and ribs down; avoid craning neck to bar.
- Squat/lunge:
  - Progress by depth, tempo, and unilateral variations. Keep knees tracking over mid-foot.
- Hinge/Glutes:
  - Emphasize full hip lockout and posterior pelvic tilt at top.

Recovery, lifestyle, and habit guidelines
- Sleep: Target 7–9 hours per night. Consistency over perfection.
- Daily movement: 6–10k steps/day or at least 20–30 min brisk walk most days.
- Mobility (post-session or evenings, 5–10 min): couch stretch, pigeon or figure-4, thoracic extensions on floor, lat doorway stretch after hangs.

Basic nutrition guidance for strength and recovery
- Protein: 1.6–2.2 g/kg bodyweight/day, spread over 3–5 meals.
- Calories: Aim for slight surplus if goal is maximal strength/muscle; otherwise maintain bodyweight. For a lean beginner, a 200–300 kcal/day surplus often helps.
- Carbs: Center ~60% of daily carbs around pre/post-training windows to support performance and recovery.
- Hydration: 30–40 ml/kg/day; add 500–750 ml around training.
- Creatine monohydrate: 3–5 g/day, any time, daily. Safe and effective for strength.
- Pre-workout snack: 60–90 min before training, combine carbs + protein (e.g., yogurt + fruit).
- Post-workout: Normal meal within 1–2 hours; emphasize protein (25–40 g) + carbs.

Objective milestones to track
- Hangs: 60s continuous dead hang by Week 6
- Push-ups: 15–25 continuous strict reps by Week 12
- Pulling: 1+ strict pull-up by Weeks 8–12; if not, controlled 6–8s eccentric for 3–5 reps is still a win
- Lower body: 12+ quality reps/side Bulgarian split squat at slow tempo by Week 12
- Core: 40–60s strong hollow hold and RKC plank

Safety and form reminders
- Maintain joint-friendly ranges; stop sets if form degrades.
- Use controlled breathing: inhale during lowers, exhale through the hard part; brace the trunk.
- Check the doorway bar’s stability every session. Avoid dynamic kipping or swinging.

This plan gives you a serious, progressive strength pathway with nothing but a mat and a doorway bar. Log reps, set targets each week, film key sets for technique review, and adjust inclines/assists to keep effort at 7–9/10 on the final set without breaking form.
